title: Pea and Ham Soup
subtitle: thick, smoky, and filling
excerpt: Frozen peas and smoked bacon make a fast version of this classic British soup. The smokiness from the bacon pairs well with the sweetness of the peas. Blending half the soup gives it body while keeping some texture.
sourceNotes: Pea and ham soup is a staple of British home cooking, historically made with a ham hock simmered for hours. This faster version uses smoked bacon and frozen peas for an everyday result.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double. Good for batch cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat gently.

content.text: For a richer soup, use a ham hock instead of bacon. Simmer it in the stock for 2 hours first, then shred the meat and use the cooking liquor as your soup base.

items.prepNote: use a ham hock or 200g smoked bacon, diced
use a handful of fresh mint leaves

content.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the bacon and cook until lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Remove half the bacon and set aside.
Add the onion to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the peas and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Blend half the soup until smooth, then stir it back in. Or blend all of it for a smoother result.
Stir in the cream and mint. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved bacon.

items.fix: Cook peas for no more than 5 minutes and blend quickly.
Simmer uncovered to reduce, or blend in extra peas.

content.text: Pea and ham has been a British pairing for a very long time. The classic slow-cooked version uses a whole ham hock, which simmers for hours and produces a deeply savoury stock. This quicker version keeps the same smokiness and sweetness without the long cooking time. It is a reliable midweek soup that fills the house with a good smell.
